\paragraph{\texttt{HighwayHash} (random $256$-bit key).}
HighwayHash~\cite{highwayhash} absorbs $32$-byte packets into four lanes of two
$64$-bit words $v_0,v_1$ and two multipliers $\mathit{mul}_0,\mathit{mul}_1$; per
lane and packet it forms the products $\mathrm{lo}_{32}(v_1)\cdot\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_0)$
and $\mathrm{lo}_{32}(v_0)\cdot\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_1)$, XORs them into the
multipliers and permutes bytes between the two words of a lane pair (``zipper
merge''); a product reaches $v_0,v_1$ only at the next packet.  The key is XORed
into public constants, $v_0=\mathit{init}_0\oplus k$, so the event
$\mathrm{hi}_{32}(k_0)=\mathrm{hi}_{32}(\mathit{init}_0[0])=\mathtt{0xdbe6d5d5}$,
of probability exactly $2^{-32}$, zeroes the first product of lane~$0$ at
packet~$1$ and leaves $v_0[0],v_1[0]$ multiplication-free functions of the key.
Our pair has three packets and differs only in lane~$0$: packet~$1$ is
$-\mathit{init}_0[0]$ resp.\ that $+2^{8}$, packet~$2$ is
$\mathtt{0xb3000100}-\mathit{init}_0[0]$ resp.\ that $-(2^{9}+2^{24})$, packet~$3$
is $0$ resp.\ $2^{8}$.  The $+2^{8}$ moves through the zipper into byte~$5$ of
$v_0[0]$ and byte~$3$ of $v_1[0]$; at packet~$2$ the lane-$0$ product $x\cdot h$
with $x=\mathrm{lo}_{32}(v_1[0])$, $h=\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_0[0])$ is unchanged iff
$x-h\equiv2^{8}\pmod{2^{32}}$, whereupon the zipper cancels the difference in
$v_0[0]$ and packet~$3$ the one in $v_1[0]$: the entire $1024$-bit state
collides, so the pair collides in HighwayHash-64, -128 and -256 and under every
common suffix.  Because $x$ and $h$ are multiplication-free the relation is not
a uniform $32$-bit event: three of its bytes cost exactly $2^{-8}$ and the top
byte, which the constant $\mathtt{0xb3000100}$ targets, holds with probability
$235\cdot239/2^{16}$, so
$\Pr[\text{collision}\mid\mathrm{hi}_{32}(k_0)=\mathtt{0xdbe6d5d5}]\ge235\cdot239/2^{40}=2^{-24.22}$
exactly (\Cref{lem:exact-trail}) and $\varepsilon\ge56165/2^{72}=2^{-56.22}$
over a uniform key: $2^{7.8}$ times the ideal $2^{-64}$, and $2^{71.8}$ and
$2^{199.8}$ times the ideal of the $128$- and $256$-bit outputs, which gain
nothing.  The count was confirmed by exhaustive runs over all $2^{32}$ values of
$\mathrm{hi}_{32}(k_1)$ at fixed remaining key bits; Monte Carlo over $19$
independent runs gave $2109$ full-state collisions in $4.35\cdot10^{10}$ keys of
the class ($2^{-24.30}$, $2.4\sigma$ below the exact value), every one a
collision at all three widths, and $0$ in $2^{28}$ unconditioned keys; the key

% Exact probability of the three-packet HighwayHash state-collision trail.
% Notation: for a 64-bit word w, w[j] is byte j (bits 8j..8j+7); lo(w), hi(w) are its 32-bit halves;
% (w_3,w_2,w_1,w_0) lists bytes 3..0 of a 32-bit word; all sums are of integers unless "mod" is written.
% Constants: I_{00}=init0[0]=dbe6d5d5fe4cce2f, I_{01}=init0[1]=a4093822299f31d0,
%            I_{10}=init1[0]=3bd39e10cb0ef593, I_{11}=init1[1]=c0acf169b5f18a8c (hex).

\begin{lemma}[exact probability of the three-packet trail]\label{lem:exact-trail}
Let $m_1,m_2$ be the 96-byte messages
\begin{align*}
m_1&=(p_1,0,0,0\mid p_2,0,0,0\mid 0,0,0,0),\\
m_2&=(p_1+2^{8},0,0,0\mid p_2-2^{9}-2^{24},0,0,0\mid 2^{8},0,0,0),
\end{align*}
(four little-endian 64-bit lanes per packet, arithmetic mod $2^{64}$), with
$p_1=-I_{00}$ and $p_2=c_2-I_{00}$, $c_2=\mathtt{b3000100}$.
Let $K=(K_0,K_1,K_2,K_3)$ be a HighwayHash key with $\operatorname{hi}(K_0)=\mathtt{dbe6d5d5}=\operatorname{hi}(I_{00})$
(condition~(1)), $\operatorname{lo}(K_0)$ and $K_1$ uniform on $\{0,1\}^{96}$ and $K_2,K_3$ arbitrary.
Let $\mathcal C$ be the event that the full 1024-bit HighwayHash state after the three packets of $m_1$
equals the state after the three packets of $m_2$ (so every suffix and every output width collides).
Then
\[
\Pr[\mathcal C]\;\ge\;\Pr[E_2]\;=\;\frac{235\cdot 239}{2^{40}}\;=\;\frac{56165}{2^{40}}\;=\;2^{-24.2226\ldots},
\]
where $E_2$ is the event $\operatorname{lo}(v_1[0])-\operatorname{hi}(v_0[0])\equiv 2^{8}\pmod{2^{32}}$ evaluated at the
lane-0 $\mathit{mul}_0$ multiplication of packet~2 (the two operands of that multiplication).
Consequently, over a uniformly random 256-bit key,
\[
\Pr[\mathcal C]\;\ge\;2^{-32}\cdot\frac{235\cdot 239}{2^{40}}\;=\;\frac{56165}{2^{72}}\;=\;2^{-56.2226\ldots},
\]
and $\Pr[E_2\mid(1)]$ exceeds the value $2^{-32}$ of a uniformly distributed 32-bit difference by the exact
factor $56165/256=219.4=2^{7.78}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\textbf{0. The round function on lanes 0,1.}
$\mathrm{Update}(p)$ first applies, lane by lane,
$v_1\mathrel{+}=\mathit{mul}_0+p$;\ $\mathit{mul}_0\mathrel{\oplus}=\operatorname{lo}(v_1)\cdot\operatorname{hi}(v_0)$;\
$v_0\mathrel{+}=\mathit{mul}_1$;\ $\mathit{mul}_1\mathrel{\oplus}=\operatorname{lo}(v_0)\cdot\operatorname{hi}(v_1)$,
and then, writing $A=v_1[0]$, $B=v_1[1]$,
$v_0[0]\mathrel{+}=Z_0(A,B)$, $v_0[1]\mathrel{+}=Z_1(A,B)$, and afterwards with $A=v_0[0]$, $B=v_0[1]$ (the
updated values) $v_1[0]\mathrel{+}=Z_0(A,B)$, $v_1[1]\mathrel{+}=Z_1(A,B)$, where (bytes $0,\dots,7$)
\begin{align*}
Z_0(A,B)&=(A[3],B[4],A[2],A[5],B[6],A[1],B[7],A[0]),\\
Z_1(A,B)&=(B[3],A[4],B[2],B[5],B[1],A[6],B[0],A[7]).
\end{align*}
Lanes 2,3 are processed identically among themselves and never touch lanes 0,1 before the finalization
permutation, so $K_2,K_3$ are irrelevant for $\mathcal C$ (they enter both states identically).

\textbf{1. The state after packet 1 of $m_1$.}
Write $k=\operatorname{lo}(K_0)$, $a=\mathtt{fe4cce2f}\oplus k$, $b=\mathtt{3bd39e10}\oplus k$
(so $b=a\oplus\mathtt{c59f503f}$; in particular $b[1]=a[1]\oplus\mathtt{50}$, $b[0]=a[0]\oplus\mathtt{3f}$).
Reset gives $v_0[0]=(0,a)$, $v_1[0]=(b,\mathtt{10e82046})$, $\mathit{mul}_0=\mathit{init}_0$, $\mathit{mul}_1=\mathit{init}_1$.
In packet 1, $v_1[0]\mathrel{+}=I_{00}+p_1=0$; the product $\operatorname{lo}(v_1[0])\cdot\operatorname{hi}(v_0[0])$ is
$0$ because $\operatorname{hi}(v_0[0])=0$ under condition~(1), so $\mathit{mul}_0[0]=I_{00}$ is unchanged; then
$V_0:=v_0[0]=a+I_{10}$ and $\mathit{mul}_1[0]=I_{10}\oplus\operatorname{lo}(V_0)\cdot b$.
In lane 1, $W_1:=v_1[1]=(I_{11}\oplus\operatorname{rot}_{32}(K_1))+I_{01}$ and
$W_0:=v_0[1]=(I_{01}\oplus K_1)+I_{11}$ (the lane-1 multipliers do not matter below).
The two zipper steps then give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:U0}
\begin{aligned}
U_0&:=v_0[0]=V_0+Z_0\big((b,\mathtt{10e82046}),W_1\big),\\
U_1&:=v_0[1]=W_0+Z_1\big((b,\mathtt{10e82046}),W_1\big),\\
T&:=v_1[0]=(b,\mathtt{10e82046})+Z_0(U_0,U_1).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $Z_0((b,\mathtt{10e82046}),W_1)=(\mathtt{10},W_1[4],\mathtt{e8},b[1],W_1[6],\mathtt{20},W_1[7],\mathtt{46})$.
Put $Z_c:=b[1]2^{24}+\mathtt{e8}\cdot2^{16}+W_1[4]2^{8}+\mathtt{10}$ (its low half) and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gamma}
\gamma:=\Big\lfloor\frac{a+\mathtt{cb0ef593}+Z_c}{2^{32}}\Big\rfloor\in\{0,1,2\},
\qquad \operatorname{lo}(U_0)=(a+\mathtt{cb0ef593}+Z_c)\bmod 2^{32}.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:h}
h:=\operatorname{hi}(U_0)=\mathtt{81d3be10}+W_1[7]\,2^{16}+W_1[6]+\gamma \pmod{2^{32}},
\end{equation}
so $h_0=(\mathtt{10}+W_1[6]+\gamma)\bmod 256$ with carry $e_0=[\mathtt{10}+W_1[6]+\gamma\ge256]$,
$h_1=\mathtt{be}+e_0\in\{\mathtt{be},\mathtt{bf}\}$, $h_2=(\mathtt{d3}+W_1[7])\bmod256$ with carry $e_2$, and
$h_3=\mathtt{81}+e_2\in\{\mathtt{81},\mathtt{82}\}$. In particular
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hbounds}
U_0[5]=h_1\ne\mathtt{ff},\qquad h<2^{32}-2^{8}.
\end{equation}
Finally $\operatorname{lo}(T)=\mathtt{10e82046}+Q\pmod{2^{32}}$ with $Q:=(h_1,U_0[2],U_1[4],U_0[3])$, since
$\operatorname{lo}(Z_0(U_0,U_1))=(U_0[5],U_0[2],U_1[4],U_0[3])$.

\textbf{2. The difference trail: $E_2\Rightarrow\mathcal C$.}
Track $m_2$ against $m_1$; all differences are modular in $2^{64}$.
\emph{Packet 1.} $v_1[0]$ differs by $+2^{8}$; its low half is the constant $\mathtt{10e82046}$, so the
difference sits in byte 1 ($\mathtt{20}\to\mathtt{21}$) and $\operatorname{hi}(v_1[0])=b$ is unchanged; both
multiplications of lane 0 use only $\operatorname{hi}(v_0[0])=0$, $\operatorname{lo}(V_0)$ and $\operatorname{hi}(v_1[0])$, so all
multipliers are equal. $Z_0(v_1[0],W_1)$ has byte 5 $=v_1[0][1]$, hence differs by exactly $2^{40}$, while

res.summary: Automated byte-level enumeration of 2-4 packet key-conditioned trails in the HighwayHash absorb phase (lane pair {0,1}; pair {2,3} is isomorphic, the zipper never mixes pairs), priced with per-byte key-dependence tracking (dead multiply = 8 bits per key-dependent byte of the zero operand, coincident multiply = 32-bit relation x-h=a when the operand differences satisfy a=-b, otherwise solution-count sampling; carry-only bytes priced at 0 = optimistic lower bounds). 18,400 shapes priced (n=3: <=2 bytes per pattern, values +-1,+-2; n=4: 1-byte packet 1, <=2-byte packet 2, packet 3 forced). RESULT: the known shape (lane-0/2 byte-1 difference, dead mul0 at packet 1 via hi32(key0)=hi32(init0[0]), coincidence x-h=delta*2^8 at packet 2) is the UNIQUE shape at or below 56.3 bits (optimistic 56.0). Runner-up: the same shape in an odd lane (72.2 bits: the odd lanes' zipper column sends byte 1 to byte 4 so Delta_h=1 vs Delta_x=2^8, a mismatched coincidence of density 2^-40.2). Every other shape needs a second dead multiply (>=76.4/80 bits), and every non-degenerate 4-packet shape prices >=80 bits because packet 3 always hits a product-contaminated operand. Structural facts: (i) at the first differing packet each affected lane's multiply sees a difference in ONE operand only, and (x+d)h=xh mod 2^64 with 32-bit operands forces h=0 (|dh|<2^64), so a dead multiply (exact 2^-32) is unavoidable and 'two 2^-24 coincidences, no dead multiply' is impossible; the multiplication-free skew of condition (2) exists only because condition (1) zeroes the packet-1 product; (ii) n=2 is impossible in the dmul=0 model; (iii) for the surviving shape the low 24 bits of x-h are exactly uniform (bijective images of key0 bytes 2,3 and key1 byte 4) and the top byte's modal probability is capped by one key-dependent carry at ~1-17/256=0.934, so the shape's ceiling is 2^-32 x 2^-24.10 = 2^-56.10. Cheapest packet-2 condition in the model (hi32(v0[0])=0, two key-dependent bytes) demonstrated at 2^-15.92 with tuned constants, but every shape using it also needs a 32-bit contaminated condition. Cheapest shape ruled out with a reason: lane-1 byte-1 at >=72.2 bits (mismatched coincidence x=2^8(h+1) has only ~2^24 solutions); all 4-packet shapes at >=80 bits. z3 (4.15.4) queries on the exact 64-bit model returned unknown/were stopped at the wall budget and are not used as evidence.

v.corrected_claim: At the first packet where the messages differ, no multiply can be 'coincident': in an affected lane each multiply sees a difference in exactly one 32-bit operand (products are exact 32x32 integers), so its product is unchanged iff the other operand is 0. Hence any trail that keeps mul0/mul1 difference-free (the dmul=0 model; product-difference cancellation is a separate, unpriced conjecture) needs a dead multiply per affected lane: hi32(v0[i])=0 for a low-half difference, lo32(v0[i]+mul1[i])=0 for a high-half difference, both (v0[i]=0, 2^-64) if both halves differ. At packet 1 these are exactly 2^-32 over a uniform key (v0 = init0 ^ key); at later packets they are heuristically 2^-32, not exact. Condition (1) hi32(key0)=0xdbe6d5d5 makes mul0[0] stay init0[0], so the packet-2 lane-0 mul0 operands x=lo32(v1[0]+mul0[0]+c2) and h=hi32(v0[0]) are both multiplication-free (h is multiplication-free in every lane regardless; x needs the condition); without condition (1) the coincidence relation's top byte is uniform (measured 2^-8.00), so the 2^-24.3-type skew requires the dead multiply first. res.label: min-length
res.summary: The third step of the HighwayHash lane-0 trail CAN be the remainder step: with the same two conditions (cond 1: hi32(key[0]) = 0xdbe6d5d5, exact density 2^-32; cond 2: the tuned relation at the packet-2 lane-0 multiply, measured 2^-24.32 over 2^33 class keys) the pair collides in the full 1024-bit state after UpdateRemainder for every s in 4..17 and 24..31 (message 64+s bytes) on exactly the same keys as the 96-byte pair, and for s = 18..23 with the rate reduced by the rotation-wrap factor 1 - 2^-(24-s) (measured 207,204,200,181,148,100 of 208). The shortest lane-0 message is 68 B (s = 4; for s <= 3 the padded packet's lane 0 is zero padding). The mirror trail in lane 2 (cond 1': hi32(key[2]) = 0x13198a2e) reaches 67 B through the three-byte copy packet[16..18], but its cond 2 costs 2^-25.18 (113 / 2^32), so on the paper's metric the 68-B lane-0 pair is the minimum: eps = 2^-56.32 at L = 8.5 words, bits = 59.40 (59.9 at 96 B; 59.48 for the 72-B pair if L must be an integer; 59.63 for the 80-B pair under the paper's multiple-of-16-bytes message model). The SECOND step cannot be the remainder step: for every class key and every second step (full packet or remainder of any length with any tail) the states differ after step 2 (proof: under cond 1 mul0 and mul1 are equal after packet 1 with certainty, v0 differs because ZipperMerge is a byte permutation, and the zipper is a bijection on (v0, v1)); sampling agrees (0 collisions). A common suffix of any length keeps the 96-B collision (411/411 at nine lengths 1..129 B) but not the 64+s-B ones (0/411: appending turns the tail into part of a full packet, parsed without size code and rotation). A common 32-B random prefix destroys the attack (0 / 2^30 class keys for the mul-kill, cond 2 and the collision), and a per-key diagnostic prefix that forces the mul-kill shows the multiplication-free skew is gone (D0 top byte flat, best bin 0.43% vs 85.6%; cond 2 1 / 2^30 instead of 2^-24.3).

Two seeds (22: 208/2^32, 23: 203/2^32); every cond-2 hit is a full 1024-bit state collision after the remainder step and a HighwayHash64/128/256 collision (public API). Explicit key dbe6d5d58afad71e a0142b42de197939 5bd2b2861106bd66 b6c304527caad524: HighwayHash64 = ffe8ab1641039aef (both), checked by a standalone build of the reference and by the Cat API. bits = log2(8.5) + 56.32 = 59.40: the paper's min over L. Packet-1 lane 2 = -init0[2], packet-2 lane 2 = 0xeb000100 - init0[2] (D2 top byte 0x15 in 49.5% of near-hits, vs 85.6% for lane 0, hence the weaker cond 2). Explicit key cfa8bd4773be32a7 2735f11c0109492e 13198a2ea8b88455 56fbe30e5cde7068: HighwayHash64 = e7e1e3d6f6d1511d (both), standalone-verified. bits = log2(8.375) + 57.18 = 60.25, worse than the 68-B lane-0 pair.

The previous panel's three-full-packet pair, re-measured on the same keys (208 + 203). It is the only variant that survives extension: all 411 collisions persist under a common random suffix of 1, 7, 16, 31, 32, 33, 64, 100 and 129 bytes (state collision after full packets). bits = 59.89.

claims.claim: Padded-packet feasibility: for the lane-0 trail the remainder step can cancel the surviving v1[0] difference iff s >= 4 (tail byte 1 for s = 4..7, byte 2 for 8..15, byte 3 for 16..23, byte 0 for 24..31); for s = 1..3 lane 0 of the padded packet is zero padding. The lane-2 mirror is feasible for s in {3, 7, 11, 15, 24..31} only (for 16 <= s <= 23 the needed byte is duplicated into lane 3 by the last-four-bytes copy). s = 1 and s = 2 are infeasible for every lane: lane 2 receives tail[0]*0x10101 resp. tail[0] + tail[1]*0x10100 and no byte differences solve d*0x10101 = 2^j or d0 + d1*0x10100 = 2^j.

Divisibility argument for s = 1, 2 in README.md.

res.caveats: (1) The per-s rows of each rem run are evaluated on the same cond-2 keys, so they are not independent samples; each row is nonetheless a measurement over the full 2^32 class keys. (2) The lane-0 seed-22 run reproduces the previous panel's 208 hits exactly (same generator, class and first two packets), so of the 411 total keys only the seed-23 half is new evidence; the combined rate 2^-24.32 carries about +-0.1 bits of Poisson uncertainty, the lane-2 rate (113 hits) about +-0.15. (3) The lane-2 constant 0xeb000100 was chosen from a window estimate (top byte 0x15 in 49.5% of near-hits); 0xec000100 (0x14, 43%) was not measured; neither reaches lane 0's 85.6%. (4) All conditional rates are sampled, not proved; only the class density 2^-32, the feasibility table, the rotation analysis and the two-step impossibility are exact. (5) The paper's L is 'message length in 64-bit words'; the 68-B value 59.40 uses L = 8.5, and the alternatives (72 B / L = 9: 59.48; 80 B / L = 10: 59.63) are given for the integer-word and multiple-of-16-bytes conventions. (8) The 2^30 run of the two-step mode was killed (66 Update calls per key on a machine at load ~300) and replaced by 2^26; the proof does not depend on it.
